action: Optimize for watch time and DM shares. Make content people want to send to friends, not just like. Track sends per reach in Insights, not just views.
impact: Instagram now ranks primarily on watch time, likes per reach, and sends per reach. Follower counts and raw views matter less. DM shares now outweigh likes for non-follower distribution.
title: Mosseri confirms 3 ranking metrics that matter

action: Make your niche obvious through captions, visuals, and audio. If people can't tell what your topic is in 2 seconds, the algorithm can't either.
impact: Topic preferences set in one surface now apply everywhere. Users who opt out of your topic become harder to reach regardless of engagement strength.
title: 'Your Algorithm' topic controls unified across Feed, Reels, Explore

action: Stop reposting. Every format needs meaningful original creation now, not just Reels. Check Account Status to see if you're flagged.
impact: Accounts posting mostly unoriginal content are excluded from Explore and recommendations. Simple edits like borders or watermarks don't count as original. 75% of US recommendations now come from original posts.
title: Original content protections extended to photos and carousels

action: Create original audio or voiceovers. Strip watermarks before cross-posting. Trending sounds still work for established accounts but hurt small ones.
impact: Reels using recycled or watermarked content get down-ranked. Original audio gets a boost. TikTok watermarks continue to suppress reach.
title: Reels favor original audio over trending sounds

action: Add relevant keywords to every video. Treat TikTok SEO like YouTube SEO now. Cover titles help click-through from search.
impact: Creators can now manually attach custom keywords to videos to improve search visibility, plus a floating Cover Title option. TikTok is doubling down on search as a discovery surface.
title: Custom search keywords for videos

action: Test longer storytelling formats. But completion rate still rules, so only go long if you can hold attention.
impact: Maximum video length raised from 3 to 10 minutes globally, making TikTok competitive with YouTube for longer content.
title: Video duration extended to 10 minutes for all creators

action: Post native, human, niche video. Keep clips tight while completion bar is high. Watch analytics weekly, don't assume last year's playbook works. Avoid AI-generated video as your main format.
impact: TikTok US sold to Oracle/Silver Lake consortium for ~$14B. The For You algorithm is being retrained on US-governed data. Reach instability during transition. Completion rate bar reportedly climbing to ~70% watched. AI-generated video now demoted.
title: US operations sold, algorithm being retrained

action: If you sell anything, make native shopping content. Even affiliate links in Shop-tagged videos get boosted.
impact: Native shopping videos get a distribution edge as the platform blends entertainment with commerce.
title: TikTok Shop content gets algorithmic priority

action: Test 60-90 second Shorts for more depth. But retention math changes, don't pad. 30-45 seconds is still the sweet spot for most niches.
impact: Shorts cap raised from 60 seconds to 3 minutes. Shorts under 60 seconds still qualify for the Shorts feed.
title: Shorts max duration extended to 3 minutes

action: Pick a niche and go deep. Make thumbnails/titles that the content actually delivers on. Use Shorts to funnel into long-form where CPMs are 10-20x higher.
impact: Browse feed now serves micro-niche clusters. Specialists rewarded over generalists. On Shorts, completion and swipe-away speed decide almost everything. CTR and watch time now judged together, clickbait titles get throttled.
title: Shorts and long-form algorithms fully separated

action: Use Shorts for discovery, long-form for revenue. Bridge Shorts viewers into full videos.
impact: YouTube keeps ~55% of Shorts ad revenue, splits remaining 45% among creators by share of monetized views. Long-form still pays significantly better.
title: Shorts monetization via Creator Pool

action: Post when your audience is most active since recency still feeds the prediction. Engagement velocity in the first hour matters more than ever.
impact: The Following feed is now sorted by Grok AI predicted engagement instead of chronological (toggle still available). Grok replaced the legacy recommendation system.
title: Following feed sorted by Grok-predicted engagement

action: Long-form video on X is now viable. Repurpose podcasts and streams.
impact: Premium subscribers can now upload videos up to 4 hours long.
title: Video upload limit raised to 4 hours for Premium

action: Cross-post your Reels to Facebook. It's free reach most people are ignoring.
impact: Facebook Reels distribution increased significantly but most creators aren't posting there.
title: Reels reach up 40%, still underused

action: Post native video on LinkedIn. Under 10 minutes, 16:9, MP4. Huge opportunity for B2B creators.
impact: LinkedIn confirmed native video posts receive significantly more distribution than text or link posts.
title: Native video gets 3x reach of text posts

action: Post only original Shorts, or add real commentary, storytelling, or unique edits to any reused clips. Voiceover descriptions, borders, and template edits no longer count as original.
impact: YouTube updated Shorts recommendations to further prioritize original content and reduce reach for re-uploaded clips without meaningful additions. Aggregator and clipping channels face reduced distribution on top of existing monetization ineligibility.
title: Shorts algorithm now prioritizes original content

action: Turn key follows into mutuals before you post, since mutuals now see and reply to you first. Reply early on your own posts to seed familiar faces at the top.
impact: X added mutual-follow data to its ranking model. Posts and replies from mutual followers get boosted visibility, and mutuals' replies now surface first in reply threads instead of strangers.
title: Mutuals boosted in posts and reply ranking

action: Make your topic unmistakable in captions, visuals, and the first seconds so Facebook can match you to users who asked for that topic. Invite followers to tap Interested or add your topic in Your Algorithm, not just like the post.
impact: Meta launched an AI-powered 'Your Algorithm' tool on Facebook on Oct 13. Users can add and manage topics in their own words via the three-dot menu and give Interested / Not interested feedback on posts, with LLMs interpreting that natural-language intent and recommendations updating in real time in the same session.
title: Facebook launches 'Your Algorithm' topic controls for Feed and Reels

action: If your profile's featured person is AI-generated, turn on the AI-generated profile label in Edit profile and check Account Status. If you are a real creator who only uses AI tools, do not add the profile label.
impact: Instagram renamed its AI creator label to 'AI-generated profile' and said profiles featuring an AI-generated person without the label can be removed from recommendations to non-followers in Reels and Explore. Profiles that add the label keep their reach, and using AI only to edit photos or write captions does not require it.
title: Undisclosed AI-generated profiles lose recommendation reach

action: Post specific lived expertise with a clear point of view only you could write. Use AI to proofread, not to generate generic posts, and check Post Analytics for 'seems like AI slop' feedback.
impact: LinkedIn's VP of Engineering said on Oct 8 that its AI-slop classifiers now cover all posts distributed beyond a poster's immediate network, at 94% precision, and views of content classified as AI slop were down 40% as of August 2026. Generic, repetitive, low-effort content gets its distribution limited, while AI assistance alone is not the target.
title: AI slop classifiers expanded to all posts beyond your network

action: Lead with Reels for discovery while this test runs. Keep making original Reels that hold watch time, and do not rely on feed posts or Stories as your first impression for new viewers.
impact: App researcher Radu Oncescu spotted a setting letting test users open Instagram directly to the Reels feed instead of the post feed, with Stories still on top and the traditional feed a swipe away. Social Media Today reported it Oct 5 and Meta confirmed to The Verge the test runs in a small number of countries; Reels already take over half of app time, so test users see short video first and feed posts and Stories later.
title: Test spotted: option to open Instagram straight into Reels

action: Cross-post your best Reels to Facebook now so you are already in the video feed if this test widens. Film vertical, hook in the first seconds, and keep captions topic-clear.
impact: TechCrunch reporting covered by PetaPixel on Oct 9 says some Facebook users in India and Indonesia now land directly in a full-screen vertical video feed when they open the app, with the classic Feed kept as a second tab and an opt-out available. Meta confirmed the test to TechCrunch and said exploring a US version next year.
title: Test spotted: Facebook opens into full-screen video for some users in India and Indonesia

action: Make Shorts that answer one clear question cleanly, with the answer spoken and shown on screen, so a viewer asking about the Short gets a satisfying result. Keep titles and spoken words matching the actual topic.
impact: YouTube announced Oct 12 via Creator Insider a limited global test putting Ask YouTube inside the Shorts player on select Shorts, English only and 18 plus, with a sparkle icon for suggested or free-form questions. The same test description mentions new mobile feeds to discover similar creators and related Shorts based on watch history, which adds a question-driven discovery path on top of the swipe feed.
title: Test spotted: Ask YouTube inside the Shorts player, plus similar-creator feeds
Creators report sudden Instagram reach drops on Oct 15
impact: Several independent creators posted on Oct 15 reporting reach fell sharply, including Dardinie Designs saying only about 1% of followers saw a recent post, Jiten Tirkey reporting reach down on Instagram and Facebook, and Rachana Mishra and Hilary Noelle posting about falling views and Reels reach. No official Meta explanation was found in the window.
action: Do not panic-change your whole format on anecdotes alone. Check your own reach per post for Oct 15-16 against your last two weeks, and keep posting original content built for watch time and sends while this is watched another day.

title: Instagram reach drops reported again on Oct 16, second day running
impact: Several independent creators posted Oct 16-17 reporting reach still down: Nanda Gita (@nandagita16, Threads, Oct 16) said Reels fell from a 200,000-600,000 average to around 60,000 and Story views fell too; Krystle Gohel (@doodlemoodart, Oct 16) posted an Insights graph showing a new post flat at near zero against her typical post climbing past 150 in 6 hours; Gleyson Assis (Oct 17 UTC / Oct 16 PT) said his dashboard showed 952.2K views in 30 days, down from September, with no violation or penalty; commenters on @ceritaibun___'s Oct 16 Threads post reported the same Story and Reel drops. This follows the Oct 15 reports already logged, so the drop is persisting a second day. No official Meta explanation was found in the window.
action: Keep posting original content built for watch time and sends, and compare your Oct 15-17 reach per post against your own last two weeks before changing format. Check Account Status for any recommendation limit.

title: Creators report TikTok views stuck in double digits and low hundreds on Oct 16-17
impact: Several independent creators posted Oct 16-17 reporting videos barely distributing: ogjestv (Facebook Reel, Oct 17 UTC / Oct 16 PT) said a video posted that morning had only 48 views despite over 800,000 followers and no rule break; Patty Jansen (Threads, Oct 16) reported consecutive zero-view videos; _kweenwen (Threads, Oct 16) and ilasebenarnya_ (Threads, Oct 17 PT) reported unusually bad views over the past two days; Alya Shae (Threads, Oct 17 PT) said posts after returning from a break are sitting at 100-200 views. A separate Oct 16 explainer from Heymikeyanda said TikTok no longer automatically gives about 200 views to new or inactive accounts. No official TikTok explanation was found in the window.
action: Do not delete and repost in a panic. Keep posting original niche videos on a steady cadence, watch whether views arrive late over 24-72 hours, and compare against your own baseline before assuming a penalty.

title: Creator reports Facebook reach down, dashboard views -19% (spotted)
impact: One named creator, Kundan Kewat (Kundan RP Vlogs, Instagram Reel posted Oct 16 PT), showed his Facebook dashboard at 184,592 views, down 19%, with engagement down 24%, and said reach has declined for many creators since around Oct 7, affecting earnings despite using content monetization. This is a single source in the window, so it is spotted, not confirmed.
action: Check your own Facebook dashboard for the last 7-14 days before acting. If your views are down similar amounts, keep posting original Reels and watch for a second day of reports.
